title: Nowhere-dense closed subsets have smaller dimension
statement: Let X be a nonempty locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] of finite dimension d [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let Z be a closed subset of X that is nowhere dense. Then the Krull dimension of Z is strictly less than d.

source.place: Tag 02P2, conclusion from the nowhere-dense closed support; finite-dimensional Noetherian dimension argument

proof.text: For every w in Z choose an affine open neighbourhood U. By [pqf-def-locnoeth] its coordinate ring is Noetherian, and [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] makes its underlying space Noetherian. Choose the irreducible component C of U containing w using [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], and take its generic point eta [def-sc-generic-point]; open subschemes of schemes are sober, as supplied by Mathlib.

If eta belongs to Z, the defining closure equality for the generic point and closedness of Z imply C is contained in the inverse image of Z in U. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-component-open], C contains a nonempty open O of U. Since U is open in X, the image of O is a nonempty open of X contained in Z, contradicting IsNowhereDense Z. Therefore eta lies outside Z and specializes to w. This argument is written completely in the Lean proof and needs no local-finiteness theorem for the global components.

Apply the proved source-library theorem topologicalKrullDim_lt_of_forall_exists_specializes (WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Topology.KrullDimension) to Z inside the ambient closed subset univ. Its hypothesis on generalizations is the preceding step. The subspace dimension bound [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and hX imply dim(univ) <= dim X = d < d+1. The theorem extends a specialization chain of length d in Z by an outside generalization, contradicting this bound, and concludes dim Z < d. It also handles Z empty and d=0. No new postponed theorem is used.
